case_selection: Post-ten-round illustration: earliest completed action in a round with an H candidate, independent of acceptance or score
expectation: Determine whether the promised glossy backsplash, black glass cooktop and metallic extractor received distinct shader settings or retain SceneAct's default roughness of 0.65 and metallic of 0. The result will determine whether a shared material-implementation verification instruction is warranted.
M_after_observation: Compared all three development pairs: bedroom chair/bed contours and restaurant pendant profiles remain substantial geometry errors, while the kitchen has relatively close background anchors but weak surface differentiation. The two read-only audits matched expectations: kitchen glass, backsplash and extractor retain roughness 0.65 and metallic 0; restaurant metal supports also retain these defaults, while its glazing successfully uses an explicit emission shader. Bedroom source likewise customizes wall color texture but leaves other surface responses at defaults. These facts establish an implementation gap, not a unique explanation of rendered brightness or proof that lower roughness improves scores. Propose a narrow H instruction connecting image-supported material intent to actual shader assignments and shared-material checks. Preserve camera/geometry priorities and existing execution policy. No new or changed M action is retained; no diagnostic render was needed. Visual benefit remains to be evaluated on Selection.
